sources.name: NIST SARD Juliet C/C++ 1.3
sources.license: CC0-1.0 / U.S. public domain (per NIST suite record)
sources.notes: NIST lists 64,099 C/C++ test cases across 118 CWEs. The official ZIP is the authoritative source-file inventory. Catalog candidates use exact .cpp archive paths; they are synthetic CWE examples, not CVEs or verified Corsair outcomes.

sources.name: Big-Vul (MSR 2020)
sources.notes: Primary dataset CSV connects CVE IDs, CWE IDs, repository commit IDs, changed files and pre/post-fix versions; published inventory has 3,754 vulnerabilities from 348 GitHub projects across 91 types. Re-resolve revisions and build dependencies before using any record.

sources.name: CVEfixes
sources.notes: Release v1.0.8 reports 11,873 CVEs, 12,107 fixing commits, 4,249 projects, 272 CWEs, and pre/post source at file and function granularity through 2024-07-23. C/C++ must be selected from language/file fields; this number is dataset-wide.

sources.name: DiverseVul
sources.license: Dataset license not stated in the primary repository; paper preprint is CC-BY-4.0
sources.notes: The paper reports 18,945 vulnerable functions, 330,492 non-vulnerable functions, 7,514 commits, and 150 CWEs. Repository metadata exposes 7,512 commit/repository URLs and notes that three commit URLs are missing. Treat source labels as candidate labels, not ground truth.

sources.name: Magma
sources.license: No top-level license file found in the reviewed v1.2 repository tree; check Magma and each upstream target before redistribution
sources.notes: Published Magma reports 118 front-ported bugs; the current documentation exposes nine target libraries and bug patch directories. It distinguishes buggy-code reached from fault condition triggered. Neither state is asserted for this catalog's target candidates.

sources.name: FuzzBench
sources.notes: The reviewed benchmarks directory contained 29 named benchmark configurations after excluding its integration script. They are project/driver candidates, not vulnerability labels; FuzzBench says it can use any OSS-Fuzz project as a benchmark.

sources.name: OSS-Fuzz
sources.notes: The project reported support for 1,000 projects and more than 13,000 vulnerabilities and 50,000 bugs as of May 2025. Those totals do not imply that every issue, reproducer, revision, or target is public and runnable; use public project configuration and disclosed issue artifacts only.
